signals.topic: Dog communication & breeding science: how dogs read us
signals.summary: A fresh cluster of science-desk pieces on how selective breeding reshaped dogs' brains to process human communication and whether a dog's listening 'talent' is born or trained.
signals.why_now: Two independent outlets published within hours: Earth.com at 2.0h ('born or trained?') and The Brighter Side of News at 5.1h ('generations of breeding changed how dogs' brains process human communication') — the freshest items in an otherwise stale, news-only pool (reddit source failed on 429, so no community corroboration). Small count, but a genuine same-day burst.

signals.topic: Decoding cat behaviour (zoomies, head-bunting, staring, laptop-sitting)
signals.summary: An evergreen, steadily-refreshed run of explainer pieces decoding everyday cat quirks — zoomies, head-rubbing, eye signals, sitting on laptops, the greeting ritual at the door.
signals.why_now: Broad, multi-outlet coverage across PetMD, The Spruce Pets, BBC Science Focus, Nine.com.au, RTE and others; most items run 900h-7000h old but the theme is evergreen, and RTE's 'is your cat loud or quiet — genes' at 93h keeps it live. In a thin news-only pool (no reddit) this is the deepest producible cluster, though it is a steady drip rather than a spike.
